display.purpose: The single headline-weight line within a component: product name, price, a state's message title, an auth page's h1 title, the cart's h2 title and its CartLineItem name/line-total/running total, and (as of slice 7a) checkout's h2 title plus each step section's own headline (ShippingForm/PaymentForm legends, each CheckoutSummaryCard title, ReviewSection's title) -- several Display strings coexist on the one continuous checkout document, but each stays scoped to its own component.

body.purpose: Descriptions and supporting copy, at 70% text opacity against ink/bone; also the catalog search input's typed value/placeholder, the detail page's curatorial note (italic), the dotted spec table, every TextField's typed value/hint/error text, PaginationControls' text-xs 'Pagina {n}' caption, CartLineItem's unit-price line, MergeExclusionsNotice's body copy, and (as of slice 7a) PaymentForm's 'no real charge' disclosure line at the same 70%-opacity cut, plus each checkout summary's confirmed-value lines at a darker 80%-opacity cut reserved for confirmed user data rather than incidental support text.

label.purpose: Piece-number badges, the retry link, the category-rail chips, the detail page's add-to-cart button label, every TextField label, the Button primitive's text (including PaginationControls' Anterior/Siguiente buttons), AuthNav's links, CartIndicator (reuses AuthNav's link class verbatim), CartLineItem's 'Quitar' control, MergeExclusionsNotice's 'Entendido' control, and (as of slice 7a) CheckoutStepIndicator's three step names in all three of their states, each CheckoutSummaryCard's 'Editar' control, and PaymentForm's 'Resultado simulado' fieldset legend; always uppercase, always 0.1em tracked.

narrative.overview: CLACK's shipped catalog is a flat grid of specimens: every product sits inside its own full-bleed field of color, badged with a piece number, and described underneath in two weights of type — a didone name/price and a grotesque description. It is the teletext half of the direction contract's museum thesis: the closed four-color field, the numbering, and the didone/grotesque split all shipped exactly as specified. The catalog's search field and category rail from the surface brief's FIRST VIEWPORT have also shipped, as a filter strip on the catalog route rather than fused into the shared header markup. The cartela and its dotted spec table have also shipped — but as a standalone product detail page reached from a card, not as the split-hero composition the brief originally described. Slice 5 added the account-facing surfaces (register, login, forgot-password, Google sign-in, logout, and an admin-access-denied state); it introduced no new color, typeface, or elevation model. Slice 4 added pagination to the catalog listing (PaginationControls): a pure application of the existing Button primitive, hairline-divider vocabulary, and established support-text pattern. Slice 6 added the cart surface (CartPage at /cart, inside the existing PublicLayout): a receipt-style list of CartLineItems, each with a closed-four-color stripe and a tabular-nums line total, closed by a running total, on the page's own theme-swapping ground like the auth pages — no fixed-tone panel. It also added a quick-add button to the Product Card itself, restructuring the card from a single full-card Link into a div wrapping a Link plus a sibling action row, because a button cannot legally nest inside an anchor. Its one structural extension to the existing vocabulary is reusing the dotted-rule divider — previously scoped to the cartela's spec table — for a second context, an itemized receipt-style list. Slice 7a added the checkout stepper (CheckoutPage at /checkout, inside PrivateLayout/ProtectedRoute): the cart and its three steps (Envio, Pago, Revision) render as one continuous growing document, never a per-step screen swap or modal, with the dotted-rule divider reused a third time to separate step sections. Its genuinely new decision resolves the base-breakpoint pinning the direction contract had left open: the step indicator becomes sticky-top and the running total becomes fixed-bottom at the base/mobile breakpoint only, both opaque with a hairline border, both resetting to in-flow layout at md:. It also extracted CartLinesSummary, a shared cart-lines-plus-total block now used by both CartPage and CheckoutPage, and gave Button an exported BUTTON_CLASSES constant so a plain Link styled as a button doesn't retype its classes. The payment step deliberately collects no card number/expiry/CVV, only a cardholder name and a forceable success/failure outcome. The review step's 'Confirmar compra' button is intentionally inert (no onClick) — order creation is deferred to a future slice, the same disclosed pattern 'Agregar al carrito' followed before it was wired. There is still no hero or landing composition anywhere in the build (that remains slice 14's work). This document records what was actually built. Depth is never simulated. There are no shadows, no gradients, and no border-radius anywhere in the sampled components — flatness is total, not partial. The dark theme (ink ground, bone text) is primary; the light theme is currently a literal swap of the same two neutrals rather than a separately-designed surface. The cartela is the one deliberate exception to theme-swapping altogether: it stays bone/ink regardless of the active theme.
keyCharacteristics: Closed four-color field system (lime, magenta, cyan, amber) — flat, full-strength, no tints or intermediate variants.
Didone (Bodoni Moda) carries the single most important line on a view; grotesque (Archivo) carries everything else.
Zero elevation: no shadows, no gradients, no border-radius anywhere in the system.
Skeletons mirror the exact shape of loaded content; no spinners.
Interactive accent color is theme-owned: magenta in light mode, cyan in dark mode, never a fixed hover color — except the one fixed-tone surface (the cartela), which never theme-swaps at all.

rules.name: The Closed Four Rule
rules.body: Only these four hexes exist as field colors anywhere in the system, enforced at the data layer by PRODUCT_DISPLAY_COLORS. No tints, no opacity variants, no fifth color.

rules.name: The Theme-Owned Accent Rule
rules.body: The interactive accent is never a fixed hardcoded hue: it is magenta in light mode and cyan in dark mode. Amber and lime are identity fields only and never carry interaction state. Now also governs Button/TextField focus-hover states, the auth pages' secondary links, the cart's quick-add/remove/dismiss controls, and (slice 7a) CheckoutStepIndicator's completed-step buttons/active-step underline and every CheckoutSummaryCard's 'Editar' control.

rules.name: The Cycled-Not-Identity Rule
rules.body: Small color swatches (product displayColor, the category-rail dot, and the CartLineItem stripe) cycle through the four closed field colors by index rather than mapping 1:1 to items. With six categories and four colors, two pairs necessarily repeat — the swatch is a scan-rhythm cue, the uppercase label is the disambiguator. Don't add a fifth color to eliminate a repeat.

rules.name: The Fixed Paper Rule
rules.body: The product detail page's cartela panel (bg-bone text-ink) is bone-on-ink unconditionally and does not theme-swap with the page's dark mode — a fixed paper object in the scene regardless of the room's lighting. Any component placed inside it must not assume the page's theme-swap reaches it. Scoped to the cartela; does not license a second fixed-tone surface elsewhere without the same editorial reason. Confirmed by slice 5, slice 6, and slice 7a: the auth pages, the cart page, and the checkout page all had the same choice and did not take it, even where checkout pins chrome to the viewport edge — pinning is a position change, not a fixed-tone-surface change.

rules.name: The One Headline Rule
rules.body: Bodoni Moda appears at most once per component as the highest-weight line — the product name, the price, or a state's message title — never for two competing strings on the same card or screen. Disclosed exception: the product detail page carries two h1s (header wordmark + cartela name), an accepted single-item-page trade-off. AccessDeniedState, CartPage, and CheckoutPage all demote their own heading to h2 to keep the strict rule. Slice 7a clarifies the rule is scoped per component, not per page: several Display headlines coexist on the one continuous checkout document (one per step section), and that's compliant because each stays the single headline within its own component.

rules.name: The Flat Ground Rule
rules.body: Surfaces never lift with a shadow. If a component needs to stand out, it gets a field color, not an elevation. Holds even for position: sticky/fixed chrome (see the Pinned Chrome Rule) — pinning changes position, never elevation.

rules.name: The Hairline-With-One-Exception Rule
rules.body: Borders default to hairline, low-opacity (ink/15 / bone/15). The catalog search input's and TextField's resting border (ink/50 / bone/40) is a deliberate, scoped exception to clear the WCAG 3:1 non-text UI-boundary contrast floor for bare-bottom-border interactive controls — not a new default border weight. Button clears the same floor differently, with a full-opacity border-current. The cartela's own hairline border is scoped to the two edges abutting page-bone only. PaginationControls, CartPage, and CheckoutPage's pinned chrome all close their respective lists/edges with this same default hairline, no new weight.

rules.name: The Border-Current Rule
rules.body: Any reusable component that might be dropped inside a fixed-tone surface (like the cartela) must use border-current/currentColor rather than a hardcoded dark: variant tied to the page's own theme-swap. Originated as a real bug fix in QuantitySelector; Button independently follows the same convention.

rules.name: The Dotted-List Rule
rules.body: The dotted divider (divide-dotted) is scoped to three confirmed contexts: dl-style spec/attribute tables (the cartela), itemized receipt-style lists (CartPage's line-item list), and sequential document sections (CheckoutPage's step sections, slice 7a). Not a general substitute for the hairline convention on arbitrary content lists.

rules.name: The Pinned Chrome Rule
rules.body: At the base/mobile breakpoint only, CheckoutStepIndicator becomes sticky top-0 and the running total (CartLinesSummary's totalVariant='sticky-bottom') becomes fixed inset-x-0 bottom-0, both with an opaque bg-bone/dark:bg-ink background and a hairline border on the edge facing the content, so content passes visibly underneath/behind them. Both reset to normal in-flow positioning at md: and up. Resolves a 'decision sin resolver' the direction contract left open. The pinning mechanism is always an opaque background plus a hairline border, never a shadow — pinned chrome still obeys the Flat Ground Rule.

dos: Do assign exactly one of the four closed field colors, full-strength and full-bleed, per product tile — and, on the product detail page, to the image panel itself, and, on the cart page, to each CartLineItem's color stripe.

Do keep Bodoni Moda to one headline-weight string per component (name, price, or state message) — never stack two didone lines competing for attention within the same component, even on a continuously-scrolling document like checkout where several components each carry their own single headline.
Do build any new skeleton to the exact shape of its loaded content, and gate its animation behind motion-safe:.
Do source interactive accent color from the active theme (magenta light / cyan dark), not a hardcoded hex — except inside the cartela's fixed-tone surface, where hardcoded colors are correct.
Do keep corners square and surfaces shadow-free; depth comes from the field color, never from elevation.

Do cycle small color swatches (category-rail dots, product displayColor, the cart line-item stripe) through the closed four-field set by index, and let the adjacent text label disambiguate — repeated colors across items are expected, not a bug.

Do keep a heavier-than-hairline border scoped to bare-bottom-border interactive controls that need it to clear a contrast floor (search input, TextField); a fully-bordered control like Button clears the same floor with full-opacity border-current instead.
Do use border-current/currentColor (not a dark: variant) in any reusable component that might be dropped inside a fixed-tone surface like the cartela — see QuantitySelector and Button.
Do use aria-labelledby referencing separate name/description/price ids for card-as-link components, following the Product Card's pattern.
Do validate forms with react-hook-form's mode: 'onTouched' and isolate live-computed per-keystroke UI state into a child component subscribed with useWatch, not the form's whole-subscribing watch().
Do share one aria-describedby slot between a field's hint and its error, hiding the hint once an error is present, when the error message already restates the hint's content.
Do reuse the stock Button primitive and its existing disabled treatment for prior/next-style controls (see PaginationControls) instead of building a bespoke state for 'can't go further'.

Do reuse the dotted-rule divider for itemized receipt-style lists and sequential document sections (see CartPage's line-item list and CheckoutPage's step sections), alongside its original dl spec-table use — a confirmed three-context pattern, not a one-off.
Do render a label-plus-count control (see CartIndicator) as a single interpolated string inside one text node, not a label text node followed by a separately-rendered count span.

Do export a primitive's className string as a named constant (see Button's BUTTON_CLASSES, AuthNav's AUTH_NAV_LINK_CLASSES) when a non-primitive element needs to look identical to the primitive without duplicating its class string.

Do use position: sticky/fixed with an opaque bg-bone/dark:bg-ink background and a hairline border (never a shadow) when pinning navigational chrome or a running total at the base/mobile breakpoint — see the Pinned Chrome Rule. Reset to normal in-flow layout at md: and up.
Do render a completed multi-step form's step as a clickable non-disabled button and an unreached step as a plain non-interactive dimmed label, not a disabled button — see CheckoutStepIndicator.
donts: Don't add border-radius, drop shadows, gradients, or glassmorphism — none exist in the shipped system and none are implied by the direction contract.
Don't introduce a tint, opacity variant, or fifth color into the closed four-field set — including as a 'fix' for a cycled swatch repeat.

Don't assume a full-width split-hero/landing composition exists just because the cartela shipped — the cartela is a standalone product detail page; the hero/landing composition remains unbuilt (slice 14).

Don't treat the current light theme (a literal ink/bone swap) as the finished 'separately designed' light mode the direction contract calls for — it is recorded here as shipped behavior, not as an approved target for future light-theme work.

Don't generalize the search input's/TextField's heavier border (ink/50 / bone/40) into the system's default border weight — it's a one-off contrast-floor exception for bare-bottom-border controls, not a replacement for the hairline convention.
Don't fold catalog-specific filtering controls into PublicLayout's shared header — it also wraps routes (product detail, auth pages, cart, checkout, future landing) that don't need them.

Don't generalize the Fixed Paper Rule into a second fixed-tone surface elsewhere without the same editorial reason — the auth pages, the cart page, and the checkout page all confirm this by staying on the page's own theme-swapping ground instead, even where checkout pins chrome to the viewport edge.
Don't wire a hardcoded dark: color pair onto a component that could end up inside a fixed-tone surface; use currentColor/border-current or an explicit non-conditional value instead.

Don't treat the product detail page's two h1 elements as a pattern to reproduce deliberately elsewhere — it's a disclosed single-item-page trade-off. AccessDeniedState, CartPage, and CheckoutPage all demote to h2 for exactly this reason.

Don't read PaginationControls' small text-xs page-label caption as a precedent for a new uppercase/tracked kicker or eyebrow treatment — it is plain Body-family support text at a smaller size, not the Label token, and no kicker/eyebrow component exists anywhere in this system.

Don't nest a button inside an anchor (or vice versa) — invalid HTML. When a card or list item needs both a navigation link and an independent action, wrap both in a container element and keep the interactive controls as siblings, not nested.

Don't use a disabled button to represent an unreached step in a multi-step flow — render it as a plain non-interactive element instead; a disabled control implies the action exists but is temporarily blocked, which isn't true for a step not yet reached.

Don't treat the payment step's absence of a card-number/expiry/CVV field as a gap to complete — it's a confirmed, scoped simplification; the spec requires only a forceable success/failure outcome, not a realistic card form.
Don't wire ReviewSection's 'Confirmar compra' button with a stub handler to make it feel functional — the inert button is the disclosed, correct state for this slice; order creation is deferred.
